review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the sibling ProfiniteCoinducedRestriction.lean, the CGCExamples/CoinducedRestriction.lean usage, and the places that use coind₁_apply_apply. The file has no @[simp] attributes at all. The one specialization in the sibling file that does carry @[simp] is a re-export of the main hom_apply. I did not run Lean. The suggestions about how simp would behave (firing order, and the round-trip lemmas becoming provable by simp from hom_apply and inv_apply) are untested. I judged change_section, section_congr and natural not to be simp lemmas: change_section would rewrite s into t and t into s, and natural is an equation of morphisms. I did not report inv_apply as a simp problem. Its statement embeds an anonymous membership proof term, which is awkward as a simp lemma, but that is a secondary point.

findings.problem: This is the canonical evaluation lemma for the forward map. It is stated as `((coind₁RestrictionIso H B s hs).hom).hom f h c = f (h.val * (s c)⁻¹)`, and the right side is strictly simpler. It has no @[simp] attribute. The closed-subgroup specialization `profiniteCoind₁RestrictionIso_hom_apply` does carry @[simp], so users of the general iso must rewrite by hand, as the file does at line 222 and line 272. The example file `CGCExamples/CoinducedRestriction.lean` also threads the lemma through `calc`/`.trans`, because `simp` cannot unfold the opaque iso.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`. The left side has head `Hom.hom (Iso.hom (coind₁RestrictionIso ...))`, with arguments `f h c` applied. The right side no longer mentions the iso, so a rewrite cannot loop. After this, `coind₁RestrictionIso_action_apply` could be derived with `simp`. Keep `coind₁RestrictionIso_change_section` out of the simp set.
findings.benefit: Downstream goals about the restriction iso would simplify to evaluation of `f` at `h * (s c)⁻¹` without naming the lemma. The general lemma would also be consistent with its simp-tagged profinite specialization.

findings.excerpt:
((coind₁RestrictionIso H B s hs).inv).hom
      (((coind₁RestrictionIso H B s hs).hom).hom f) = f
findings.problem: These two round-trip lemmas are exactly the simp-normal cancellation rules for the iso, `inv (hom f) = f` and `hom (inv f) = f`. They are not tagged @[simp] (the second is at lines 199–209). Both are proved by an awkward `change ... ≫ ...; rw [hom_inv_id]; rfl`. Goals mixing `.hom.hom` and `.inv.hom` of this iso are not reduced by the file's simp set. The lemmas appear to be unused in the repository, so no downstream proof benefits from them.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `coind₁RestrictionIso_inv_hom_apply` and `coind₁RestrictionIso_hom_inv_apply`. Both have strictly smaller right sides (`f`) and so cannot cycle. If both `hom_apply` and `inv_apply` become simp lemmas, check that the round-trip lemmas still fire first. The simp priority of the round-trip lemmas, or the order in which the apply lemmas unfold, may need adjusting. In particular the `inv_apply` statement with an embedded membership proof could unfold `.inv.hom f t` before the cancellation applies. If so, give the round-trip lemmas higher priority.
findings.benefit: Compositions of the forward and inverse maps would collapse to the identity automatically, instead of requiring hand-written `change`/`rw` steps.
